decisions.reason: The source grants placement flexibility for the integrated one-board variant and contrasts it with the earlier three-board design; it does not change the connector-placement rules scoped to the three-board variant.
The integrated one-board variant and absence of interboard connectors are already represented in the candidate state; this source changes connector-placement flexibility rather than architecture.
The general placement flexibility remains subject to the antenna direction and keepout constraints established immediately before the source message.
This candidate governs the separate power board, while the source concerns connector placement on the integrated one-board variant.
The source addresses placement of connectors and does not alter breakout pin coverage, pitch, format, or breakout-hole placement.

The source does not mention or revise the separate task-local enclosure specification; applying the integrated-board change to that enclosure would require an additional client decision about which board variant the enclosure must support.
The candidate concerns fitting required content on the separate sensor board, whereas the source grants placement flexibility for components associated with the integrated-board design.
The source does not modify the dimensions or routing-space requirements of the earlier separate main board.
Connector-placement flexibility on the integrated board does not change the separate power board's layer count or grounding requirement.
The source changes where connectors may be placed, not their sourcing, availability, cost, assembly status, or JLCPCB component classification.
The interboard power interface remains scoped to the three-board variant; the source's description of the integrated variant does not revise that variant-specific interface.
The source grants positional flexibility but does not change the requirement to use through-hole connector mounting.
